Area.evidence_source: A history of childhood physical or sexual abuse was very common among the men in this study. Men who had been abused as children linked their current mental health problems to these experiences but noted that physicians did not assess, discuss, and/or appreciate the long-term consequences of abuse to current mental health problems. These experiences were linked to an inability to trust others and/or to develop supportive and intimate relationships. Perceived failure on the part of health care providers to enquire about or give credence to the impact of childhood abuse contributed to the negative health care experiences of these men.
